'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***[[Gaza humanitarian crisis (2023–present)|Gaza humanitarian crisis]]
****Eleven [[Palestinian]]s, including the director of Gaza's Ambulance and Emergency Department, are killed in [[Israel]]i airstrikes on the [[al-Shati refugee camp]], [[Bani Suhaila]], and [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-kills-senior-gaza-health-official-tanks-push-deeper-into-rafah-2024-06-24/ (Reuters)]
**[[Three-phase Israel–Hamas war ceasefire proposal]]
***[[Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] rejects the U.S.-backed [[ceasefire]] proposal for the war in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], instead committing to continuing the war and "the goal of eliminating [[Hamas]]." [https://time.com/6991146/netanyahu-rejects-permanent-ceasefire-israel-gaza/ (TIME)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***At least four people are killed and 40 others are injured when Russian [[9K720 Iskander#Iskander-M|Iskander-M]] [[ballistic missile]]s hit [[Pokrovsk, Ukraine|Pokrovsk]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/at-least-4-dead-34-wounded-after-russian-missile-attack-on-pokrovsk/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-missiles-kill-four-wound-34-eastern-town-pokrovsk-ukraine-says-2024-06-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Dagestan attack]]
**The death toll from the attack on a synagogue and [[Eastern Orthodoxy|Orthodox]] church in [[Derbent]] and [[Makhachkala]], [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]], yesterday, increases to 20, with 46 others injured. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russias-dagestan-mourns-priest-police-killed-attack-by-gunmen-2024-06-24/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Aricell battery factory fire]]
**Twenty-three people are killed and eight others are injured in a fire at a [[lithium-ion battery|lithium battery]] factory in [[Hwaseong, Gyeonggi|Hwaseong]], [[Gyeonggi]], [[South Korea]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/about-20-bodies-found-after-fire-south-korea-battery-plant-yonhap-reports-2024-06-24/ (Reuters)]
*Eight people are killed in a fire in an office building in [[Fryazino]], [[Moscow Oblast]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8444kxgrkeo (BBC News)]
*Officials in [[Blue Earth County, Minnesota|Blue Earth County]], [[Minnesota]], United States, issue an evacuation warning due to flooding on the [[Blue Earth River]] breaching the [[Rapidan Dam]], pushing it into an "imminent failure condition" upstream of several cities. Flooding also collapses a [[railroad bridge]] connecting [[South Dakota]] and [[Iowa]] and kills two people. [https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/rapidan-dam-fails-evacuation-blue-earth-county/ (WCCO-TV)] [https://apnews.com/article/severe-weather-floods-extreme-heat-71b740c16ad97edd90b3e9422672a61e (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*The [[Royal Zoological Society of Scotland]] reports that [[Scottish wildcat]] kittens have been born in the [[Cairngorms National Park]], in a "major milestone" for the conservation of the [[critically endangered]] population. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/article/2024/jun/24/wildcat-kittens-birth-cairngorms-national-park (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Philippine drug war]]
**[[Regional Trial Court|Trial courts]] in [[Metro Manila]], [[Philippines]], dismiss the remaining charges filed against former [[Senate of the Philippines|senator]] [[Leila de Lima]] during the [[presidency of Rodrigo Duterte]], including the last of the three involving her alleged [[conspiracy]] in [[Illegal drug trade in the Philippines|the illegal drug trade]], as well as another on her disobedience to a [[summons]] for a [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House]] hearing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqeeeq8r18go (BBC News)]
*[[WikiLeaks]] founder [[Julian Assange]] enters a plea deal with the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]], in which he will be found guilty on one federal charge in exchange for his release back to [[Australia]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/wikileaks-founder-julian-assange-expected-plead-guilty-us/story?id=111380617 (ABC News)]
*A [[mass shooting]] in two apartments in North [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], United States, killed six people, including the 47-year-old gunman, Eric Adams. 13-year-old Olivia Munoz was wounded in the shooting.[https://www.gunviolencearchive.org/incident/2949852?__cf_chl_tk=bqfevKpNSgxGd__Yp5eBPru8ZyHzmRpuUXIc0Kb5I5Y-1719853091-0.0.1.1-5418 (GVA)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 New Caledonia unrest]]
**Violence and riots resume in [[New Caledonia]] after eight pro-independence activists were flown to [[France]] for [[pre-trial detention]] yesterday. Protesters burn [[National Police (France)|police]] vehicles, block roads, and set fire to the town hall in [[Koumac]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/24/fresh-violence-sparked-by-new-caledonia-independence-activists-extradition (Al Jazeera)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023–24 NHL season]]
**In [[ice hockey]], the [[Florida Panthers]] defeat the [[Edmonton Oilers]] in seven games to win the [[2024 Stanley Cup Final]], marking their first [[Stanley Cup]] championship in franchise history. The Panthers also avoid becoming the fifth team in [[National Hockey League]] history to lose a series despite having a [[List of teams that have overcome 3–0 series deficits|3–0 series lead]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2024/06/24/florida-panthers-stanley-cup-champions-game-7-edmonton-oilers/ (''The Washington Post'')]
